title: The {5, 8} funnel
W: Replace n by the sum of the largest prime factors of n and n + 1. Every start tested falls into the loop 5 → 8 → 5. Prove all do.
M: Let $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$ (with $P(1)=1$). Prove every orbit of $f$ on $n\ge2$ enters the cycle $\{5,8\}$.

title: Doubling minus one
W: Replace n by twice its largest prime factor minus one. Every tested start ends in 5 ↔ 9 or in the loop 37 → 73 → 145 → 57 → 37. Prove there is nothing else.
M: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto 2P(n)-1$ on $n\ge2$ enters $\{5,9\}$ or $(37,73,145,57)$.

title: Two long loops
W: Replace n by P(3n + 1) + P(n). Every tested start ends in one of two long loops, through 46 or through 80. Prove there are no others.
M: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(3n+1)+P(n)$ on $n\ge2$ enters the 9-cycle through 46 or the 7-cycle through 80.

title: Gerver's constant has unbounded partial quotients
W: Show the continued fraction of Gerver's sofa area contains arbitrarily large terms.
M: Prove the continued fraction expansion of $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ has unbounded partial quotients.

title: Three large consecutive factors
W: Show infinitely many n have n, n + 1 and n + 2 each with a prime factor bigger than n^0.9.
M: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $\min\{P(n),P(n+1),P(n+2)\}>n^{0.9}$.

title: A mixed Fermat equation
W: Show the equation x² + y⁴ = z⁷ + 7 has only finitely many integer solutions.
M: Prove $x^2+y^4=z^7+7$ has finitely many solutions in integers.

title: Squares of seven-free primes
W: Show every large number of the right residue is a sum of five squares of primes without the digit 7.
M: Prove every sufficiently large $n\equiv5\pmod{24}$ is $p_1^2+\dots+p_5^2$ with all $p_i$ prime and free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Square-sum 4-cycle factors
W: Split 1 to N into groups of four arranged in a cycle, so each pair of neighbours in a cycle sums to a square.
M: Prove $S_N$ has a $C_4$-factor for all sufficiently large $N\equiv0\pmod4$.

title: Additive energy of largest prime factors
W: Count quadruples with P(a) + P(b) = P(c) + P(d) among a, b, c, d up to N. Find the asymptotic.
M: Determine the asymptotics of $E(N)=\#\{(a,b,c,d)\in[N]^4: P(a)+P(b)=P(c)+P(d)\}$.

title: Cops on square sums
W: Show a bounded number of cops can catch a robber on the square-sum graph, however large N is.
M: Prove $\sup_N c(S_N)<\infty$ for the cop number of the giant component of $S_N$, and determine it.

title: Global convergence of P(n)+P(n+k)
W: For each shift k, the map n ↦ P(n) + P(n + k) seems to fall into finitely many loops. Decide whether there is an algorithm that tells, for each k, whether every orbit is eventually periodic.
M: Decide whether $\{k\ge1:$ every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(n+k)$ is eventually periodic$\}$ is recursive.

title: Pythagorean triangles of legs
W: Find infinitely many triples where every pair is the two legs of an integer right triangle, with all three numbers below a polynomial in the smallest.
M: Prove infinitely many $a<b<c$ with $a^2+b^2,\ a^2+c^2,\ b^2+c^2$ all squares and $c\le a^{C}$ for a fixed $C$.

title: Prime-sum graph and perfect codes
W: Decide for which n the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n has a set of vertices that dominates every vertex exactly once.
M: Determine all $n$ for which the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ has a perfect code (efficient dominating set).

title: Spectral radius of the prime-sum graph
W: Find the largest eigenvalue of the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n, asymptotically.
M: Prove $\lambda_1$ of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ is $\sim c\,n/\log n$ and determine $c$.

title: Number of square-sum colourings
W: Count proper colourings of the square-sum graph with a fixed number of colours. Find the exponential growth.
M: For fixed $q\ge\chi(S_\infty)+1$, prove $\lim_N\frac1N\log P_{S_N}(q)$ exists and compute it, where $P$ is the chromatic polynomial.

title: Primes in the {5,8} funnel's tree
W: Look at which starting numbers reach 5 versus 8 first under n ↦ P(n) + P(n+1). Show both happen for a positive fraction of starts.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$, prove both $\{n:$ the orbit first meets the cycle at $5\}$ and $\{n:$ first at $8\}$ have positive lower density.

title: Packing density of Gerver's sofa
W: Find the densest way to pack copies of Gerver's sofa shape in the plane, and show the density is not a rational multiple of an algebraic number.
M: Let $\delta_G$ be the translative-and-rotational packing density of Gerver's sofa. Prove $\delta_G\notin\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$.

title: Two-corner sofa
W: Find the largest shape that can turn left and then right through two consecutive right-angle corners separated by distance d.
M: For hallway width 1 and corner separation $d$, determine $\alpha(d)$ and prove $\alpha(d)$ is strictly increasing and real-analytic in $d$ on $(1,\infty)$.

title: Unit distances in the hat tiling
W: Find the largest number of unit distances among n points chosen from the vertices of the hat tiling.
M: Determine the order of $\max\{\#\{(x,y)\in A^2:|x-y|=1\}:A\subset V_{\mathrm{hat}},|A|=n\}$.

title: Hat tiling Schrödinger operators
W: Show the discrete Laplacian on the hat tiling has Cantor spectrum.
M: Prove the spectrum of the graph Laplacian of the hat-tiling dual graph is a Cantor set of zero Lebesgue measure, or show it contains an interval.

title: Rotation-proof lattice-point-poor shapes
W: Find the shape in the plane with given area that contains the fewest integer lattice points after any rotation, asymptotically.
M: Determine the convex $K$ of area $A$ minimising $\sup_{\theta}\#(\rho_\theta K\cap\mathbb{Z}^2)$, asymptotically as $A\to\infty$, to second-order term.

title: Minimal Steiner tree for prime points
W: Place points at (p, q) for primes p, q up to N. Find the shortest network connecting them asymptotically.
M: Prove $\mathrm{SMT}(\{(p,q):p,q\le N\text{ prime}\})\sim cN^2/\log N$ and determine $c$.

title: Ising model on the spectre tiling
W: Find the exact critical temperature of the Ising model on the spectre tiling graph, and prove the interfaces converge to SLE(3).
M: For the nearest-neighbour Ising model on the spectre-tiling vertex graph, determine $\beta_c$ and prove critical interfaces converge to $\mathrm{SLE}_3$.

title: Percolation threshold of the square-sum graph
W: Keep each edge of the square-sum graph with probability p. Find the exact threshold for a giant component as N grows.
M: For bond percolation on $S_N$ with $p=c/\sqrt N$, determine $c^*$ such that a component of size $\Theta(N)$ appears w.h.p. iff $c>c^*$.

title: Random greedy square-sum path
W: Build a path through 1 to N by always stepping to a random unused neighbour summing to a square. Find the expected length.
M: Determine $\lim_N\mathbb{E}[L_N]/N$ for the random greedy path in $S_N$ started at a uniform vertex.

title: First-passage percolation on primes
W: Give each integer point (a, b) a random weight, but only points where a + b is prime can be used. Find the shape of the ball.
M: For FPP on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ restricted to sites with $a+b$ prime and i.i.d. Exp(1) weights, prove a shape theorem exists and show the limit shape is not a diamond.

title: Random digit deletion
W: Repeatedly delete a random decimal digit of a number until it is prime or has one digit. Find the probability of ending at a prime from a typical large start.
M: For uniform $n\le x$ and random single-digit deletions, prove $\Pr(\text{the process meets a prime})\to c$ and determine whether $c<1$.

title: Doubled prime map with a 1231 loop
W: Map n to twice its largest prime factor plus the largest prime factor of n + 1. Starts below 150,000 reach either a five-step loop through 93 or a three-step loop through 1231. Prove there are no other fates.

title: Triple factor map minus two
W: Map n to P(n) + P(n+1) + P(n+2) − 2. Tested starts reach the fixed points 8 or 33, a 13-step loop through 20, or a 9-step loop through 177. Prove nothing else happens.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)+P(n+2)-2$, prove every orbit reaches $\{8\}$, $\{33\}$, the 13-cycle through $20$, or the 9-cycle through $177$.

title: The Jacobian conjecture for degree 3 in dimension 3
W: Show every polynomial map of three-space of degree at most 3 with Jacobian determinant 1 is invertible.
M: Prove every $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\deg F\le3$ and $\det JF\equiv1$ is an automorphism.

title: Prime Nim Grundy growth
W: Find how fast the largest Grundy value of Prime Nim up to N grows.
M: Prove $\max_{n\le N}G(n)\asymp N^{\alpha}$ (or $(\log N)^\beta$) and determine the exponent.

title: Seven-free powers of three
W: Show only finitely many powers of 3 have no 7 among their decimal digits.
M: Prove $\#\{n:7\notin 3^n\}<\infty$ and determine the largest such $n$.

title: Primes with digit sum equal to a prime in two bases
W: Show a positive proportion of primes have prime digit sum in base 2 and base 3 simultaneously, relative to the expected count.
M: Prove $\#\{p\le x:s_2(p),s_3(p)\text{ both prime}\}\asymp\frac{x}{\log x(\log\log x)^2}$.

title: Treewidth of the prime-sum graph
W: Find the treewidth of the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n asymptotically.
M: Prove $\mathrm{tw}(\Pi_{2n})\sim c\,n$ for the prime-sum graph and determine $c$.
